To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a delayed state extended information filter can maintain a consistent pose estimate for long periods of time in an outdoor setting and (b) the consistency of the pose estimates is sufficient to allow the assertion of pose constraints for loop closing.

(1) the delayed state extended information filter provides a consistent pose estimate for long loops, which is good enough to guarantee assertion for vision-based loop closing; and (2) the loop closure test we propose, which combines closeness of means with the informativeness of updates, is a good way to decide whether a pose constraint should be added to the estimator, even in the presence of outliers.

(i) vision-based loop closure can be performed in the presence of delayed state information, provided no necessary links are added to maintain consistency; and (ii) a test based on both the closeness of the means and the information gain of the update can be used to assert loop closure constraints in the presence of delay.
